title: Unify request-assembler lifecycle with local-prefix cache coordinator and bump proto/grpc deps
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Context: The request-assembly layer (responsible for composing incoming RPC payloads into continuous-batch jobs) and the local-prefix cache coordinator (manages short-lived per-request prefix/state caching) have drifted. We have several overlapping lifecycles: global timers that prune inflight contexts, a coarse-grained lock protecting both assembler queues and cache metadata, and divergent tracing tags that make it hard to link a stalled assemble request to cache eviction events. This has caused sporadic tail latency spikes during high-concurrency chat workloads and increases complexity for scheduler maintenance.

Goal: Reconcile the lifecycles so assembler worker queues and the cache coordinator share a clear ownership model, remove the single global mutex in hot paths, introduce sharded cache bookkeeping, upgrade protobuf and gRPC deps to the supported house baseline, and add focused benchmarks and end-to-end canary rollout steps. The work should reduce 99.9th percentile enqueue-to-first-token latency by at least 15% on our long-context chat test, and prevent mutex contention in the assemble path observed in recent flamegraphs.
acceptance_criteria: Assembler no longer holds the single global lock in the hot enqueue path (verified by code review and flamegraph diff)
Sharded cache bookkeeping implemented with per-shard timers replacing global prune timer
Protobuf runtime bumped to v3.21 (or later) and grpc bumped to v1.58 (or later) with successful CI green builds
End-to-end benchmark shows >=15% reduction in P99 enqueue latency on long-context chat workload compared to baseline
Canary rollout plan established and executed with automated rollback on error rates or latency regressions
Observability: new traces linking assemble request ID to cache-prune events and a dashboard showing lock-wait time per function
implementation_notes: Introduce RequestAssemblerLifecycle that owns lifecycle transitions (init, warm, drain, retire) and exposes a lightweight Handle for workers
Replace global mutex with a dual-layer scheme: per-queue spinless MPSC queue + sharded cache mutex (16 shards default)
Migrate global timer to per-shard std::chrono-abseil timers to reduce wake storms during high scale
Add a thin compat shim for old protobuf IO helpers to ease migration; run codegen on all models after bump
Run full integration tests with traffic replay from production day-0 capture (sanitized) to validate behavior under realistic concurrency
Document fallback: if new snapshotting causes regressions, we will toggle to legacy path via runtime flag for 48h while investigating
plan: Week 1: Design doc and informal review with runtime and infra teams; identify hotlines and compile list of call-sites for global mutex
Week 2: Implement RequestAssemblerLifecycle and per-shard cache bookkeeping; add unit tests for lifecycle transitions
Week 3: Bump protobuf/grpc deps, fix compile-time breakages and run full CI; add perf microbench harnesses
Week 4: Run cluster-scale perf jobs, compare flamegraphs, iterate on lock removal; add tracing tags and dashboard panels
Week 5: Canary rollout to 5% of serving fleet with automated SLO gates; monitor for 72 hours before full rollout
Post-rollout: Retrospective and follow-up cleanups (remove legacy flags, tighten shard count based on telemetry)
